label: What has lamed three of the sheep in the paddock?
quote: three of them have gone lame, sir

possibilities.value: an ordinary ailment, of no account
someone cut their legs on purpose, practising for the horse

reasoning.text: Holmes expected something amiss with the sheep and calls the lameness a 'singular epidemic'. Straker died beside the horse holding a cataract knife, a blade for very fine cuts. Someone may have tried such a cut on the sheep's legs before trying it on the horse.

label: Who lamed the sheep in the paddock?
quote: this singular epidemic among the sheep

possibilities.value: nobody: it is a natural ailment

reasoning.text: The paddock lies by Straker's villa, and he carried a cataract knife. Anyone practising on the sheep over several days had to belong at King's Pyland and come and go unnoticed.
Only someone who belongs there could reach the paddock sheep again and again without being remarked.

label: Why did the stable dog make no noise in the night?

possibilities.value: the man who came in the night was someone the dog knew

reasoning.text: A guard dog gives the alarm at strangers. It was let loose on the stranger that very evening, yet nobody heard it when the horse was taken. So whoever came to the stable later was familiar to it.

possibilities.value: the dog was drugged or shut away

reasoning.text: The watchman was drugged. The dog may have been dealt with too.

value: the dog barked, but the lads slept through it

reasoning.text: The horse left the hollow alone; nobody led it away. If Straker was in the hollow cutting at the horse's leg by the light of a match, as the knife, the candle and the lamed sheep suggest, the horse itself may have lashed out and struck him on the head.

The dog stayed silent, so the man who came for the horse was one it knew, most likely Straker with his own key. He would need the lad asleep, and only Hunter's portion of the curry from his house held opium.

set.pick: he meant to return the horse, then decided to keep it
he found the horse loose and took it in

his only hope of mercy is to produce the horse safe
